info.name: Operation Golden Keyboard
info.description:
End-to-end proof that the backend enforces the competition rules on its own.

**Run the folders in order against a fresh `python manage.py seed_demo`.** Folder 0 captures every token and id into the environment, so nothing below it hardcodes a URL or an id.

Folder 8 (rate limiting) should run last -- see its description.

The seven required cases are tagged `[required case N]` in the request names.

item.name: 8. Rate limiting
item.description:
Run this folder LAST.

The claim throttle is 5 attempts per minute per user and counts failed attempts, so this folder deliberately exhausts bob's quota.

**Before re-running the whole collection, restart the server** (`Ctrl+C`, then `python manage.py runserver`) **or wait 60 seconds.** The throttle counters live in the server's local-memory cache, so re-seeding the database does not clear them -- and folder 5's 'Bob claims same mission (409)' would get 429 instead.

Alternative to the pre-request script: run the single request below six times in the Collection Runner and watch the sixth return 429.

item.name: Claim spam - 6th attempt in a minute (429)  [required case 7]

request.description: The pre-request script fires five claim attempts as bob; this request is the sixth. The throttle is scoped to the claim action only, so no other endpoint is affected.

exec: // Fire five claim attempts before this request runs, so that the request
// itself is the sixth within the same minute and must be throttled.
// The target is a mission bob has already claimed, so every attempt fails
// harmlessly with 409 -- failed attempts still consume throttle quota, which
// is exactly the behaviour being demonstrated.
console.log("Fired " + attempts + " warm-up claim attempts as bob.");
